title: Energy isolation and verification boundaries
audience: Cleaners who work on or near plant where energy isolation is required.
learningOutcomes: Explain why isolation of energy sources is done by an authorised person, not the cleaner.
Identify the energy sources that need isolation before cleaning plant.
Refuse to clean or enter plant until isolation has been verified by the authorised person.

instruction.heading: Energy sources
instruction.body: Plant can hold energy that is not obvious: electrical supply, stored pressure, hydraulic and pneumatic lines, gravity-held loads, stored heat and moving parts that coast after switch-off. Before cleaning plant, the authorised person must identify and isolate these sources, and verify that they are isolated.

instruction.heading: Verification
instruction.body: Isolation is verified, not assumed. Switching off a control is not isolation. The national plant code treats a lock as the effective isolation device, not a tag alone, and its lock-out procedure includes a trial restart (instrument dated 17 December 2015). The authorised person checks that the energy is removed, and that the machine cannot be restarted while the work is done. Only after verification does the cleaner work, and then only within the agreed area.

instruction.heading: The cleaner's boundary
instruction.body: A cleaner does not isolate or verify plant on their own authority. The national plant code expects each worker doing cleaning to hold their own lock at an isolation point, under a documented isolation procedure, so a cleaner applies a lock only where the person in control of the plant has set up that procedure and authorised it. Otherwise, refuse to clean or enter plant that has not been verified isolated, and refer the request to the authorised person. Record the request, the status and the time. This lesson does not grant any licence, certificate, plant-safety approval or specialist authority, and completing it does not make a cleaner a specialist.

procedure: Identify the energy sources that need isolation before cleaning plant.
Confirm the authorised person has isolated and verified the sources.
Do not clean or enter plant until verification is confirmed.
Refer any request to clean unisolated plant.
Record the status, the request and the time.

workedExamples.situation: A supervisor says the machine is off, so you can clean inside it now.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not enter. Switching off a control is not isolation, and the energy may still be present. Ask the authorised person to isolate and verify the machine. Record the request and the status.

equipmentAndPpe: PPE as set by the site.

commonErrors.error: Treating an off switch as isolation.
commonErrors.prevention: Only verified isolation makes plant safe to enter.

commonErrors.error: Cleaning inside a machine with stored energy.

commonErrors.prevention: Refer isolation to the authorised person.

knowledgeChecks.question: The machine is switched off. Can you clean inside it?
options: Yes, it is off, so the machine is safe to clean now
No, until the authorised person has isolated and verified it
Yes, quickly, before the machine is switched on again

knowledgeChecks.question: Which is an energy source that may remain on plant?
options: Only the mains cable and its plug
Nothing once switched off and left to stand
